description: Iteration-1 FIND-008 had two parts: (a) HEAL must check cron/log freshness, and (b) on HEAL-NEEDED the spec requires 'auto-fix (re-auth via email-OTP, restart, rollback) or ONE escalation' (design spec section 11 point 0). Part (a) is now fixed (loop.sh:72-76, see FIND-011 for a residual test-coverage caveat on this exact check). Part (b) remains unimplemented: on any HEAL-NEEDED condition (Capafy auth down, Stripe key missing/not-live, Capafy loop stale/never-ran), loop.sh only writes a suggested manual-fix string into STATE.md/HEAL (loop.sh:30, 40, 75-76) and the one-line stdout summary (loop.sh:104) — there is no auto-fix action taken and no escalation (e.g. Telegram ping) sent anywhere in the file. This is the same gap named in the spec's own motivating incident (section 8/12: 'the cron does not point at daily_loop.sh -> it never ran' went unnoticed for 6 weeks) — a STATE.md file nobody reads is exactly as silent as a log nobody reads, unless something pings a human/agent on HEAL-NEEDED.

evidence.snippet:
HEAL=""; add_heal(){ HEAL="$HEAL$1; "; }
... add_heal "STRIPE-KEY-MISSING" ...
... add_heal "CAPAFY-LOOP-STALE(...)... "
(no notification/escalation call anywhere in the file; STATE.md is the only sink)

fix: Either wire a lightweight escalation (e.g. shell out to the existing Telegram-ping pattern used by the money-path-monitor skill) when HEAL is non-empty, or explicitly amend the design spec to descope auto-fix/escalation for this measurement-only harness (as a deliberate, documented narrowing) and rely on a human/agent reading STATE.md each wake.
